paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2012 - Mechanism design for finding experts using locally constructed social referral web
title: Mechanism Design for Finding Experts Using Locally Constructed Social Referral Web
motivation: Existing social referral work assumes voluntary participation, but most paths terminate because users lack sufficient motivation to relay messages. Users are selfish and rational.
problem_framing: Truthful mechanism design for expert finding via locally constructed referral chains, where each user has privately known participation cost.
key_insight: A bonus payment equal to the gap between best and second-best scores makes truth-telling a dominant strategy while optimizing path similarity.
method_signature: Score function η_k = d^k + (1 - s_{k,t}), bonus b^k = η_x - η_k, selects minimum η neighbor locally.
evaluation_criteria: Success rate (90-95% vs 20% baseline), median path length (6), total budget cost (20% of untruthful).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Theorem 1 proof omitted; future work needed for finding groups of experts; ProdScore achieves lower per-hop cost but longer paths.
evidence_for_taste: only parameter governing success is probability of termination
proof is omitted due to space limit
bonus will not incur significant extra pay
most paths were terminated because participants are not sufficiently motivated
untruthful mechanism could be potentially unbounded
thinking_moves: 把自愿参与假设替换为自私理性参与者假设
用激励相容约束替换最优路径约束
将社会网络拓扑问题转化为机制设计问题
